patterns: APPSC asks direct one-liners: basic functional unit of ecology, first trophic level members (phytoplankton, vent bacteria, seaweeds), sequence of energy flow, secondary productivity definition, ecological pyramids as expression of trophic levels.
Recurring APPSC keys: niche statements (both true), fundamental niche, carrying capacity definition, natality statements, standing crop/biomass, producers in terrestrial ecosystems.

Traps: grazing chain starting with dead leaves, missing herbivore level, 'generating synthetic chemicals' as an environment function, inverted pyramids (pond biomass, parasitic/tree numbers), energy pyramid never inverted.
Other-PSC PYQs add biomagnification (top predator), lichen/mycorrhiza partners, halophyte/xerophyte/hydrophyte terms, insectivorous plants and nitrogen-poor soil.
App MCQs lean heavily on UPSC-style multi-statement items and long match lists; APPSC itself prefers short single-fact items with simple 2-statement or A-R forms.
App adds depth not seen in APPSC PYQs (ecogeographic rules, decomposition steps, ocean zones, r/K selection) - acceptable but should not crowd out basic definitions.
